places.name: Santa Sofia, Venice
places.what: Baptised in the parish of Santa Sofia as Barbara Valle, daughter of Isabella Garzoni; the register names no father. Her birth date is unknown. The point marks the church. It does not mark a house.

sources.title: Beth L. Glixon, “Strozzi, Barbara”, Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani 94 (2019)
Wikipedia coordinate record: Santa Sofia, Venice

places.name: Giulio Strozzi’s house, Venice
places.what: From 1634 she sang in her adoptive father’s house, where Imperiale heard her in November 1635 and the Accademia degli Unisoni met from 1637. Giulio’s will of 1650 records that the house where he lived was rented by Barbara. Her residence there for the whole period is inferred from these records; the house has not been located, and the point marks Venice.

sources.title: Beth L. Glixon, “Strozzi, Barbara”, Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani 94 (2019)
Wikipedia coordinate record: Venice

places.name: Accademia degli Unisoni, Venice
places.what: Giulio Strozzi founded the academy in 1637. Barbara performed with other musicians, acted as mistress of ceremonies at some debates and recited the discourses of the Contesa del canto e delle lagrime. The Veglie, dedicated to her, and the Contesa were printed in 1638.

sources.title: Beth L. Glixon, “Strozzi, Barbara”, Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani 94 (2019)
Mario Ruffini, “Barbara Strozzi nel Novecento” (Centro Studi Luigi Dallapiccola, 2005), pp. 221–222 and bibliography

places.name: Venice, Il primo libro de’ madrigali
places.what: Her first book, for two to five voices to texts by Giulio Strozzi, printed by Alessandro Vincenti and dedicated to Vittoria della Rovere, Grand Duchess of Tuscany.
places.work: Il primo libro de’ madrigali, Op. 1

sources.title: Beth L. Glixon, “Strozzi, Barbara”, Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani 94 (2019)
IMSLP: Madrigali, Op. 1 (Venice: Alessandro Vincenti, 1644)

places.name: Venice, Cantate, ariette e duetti
places.what: Her second book, printed by Gardano and dedicated to the Emperor Ferdinand III; the dedication is dated Venice, 1 June 1651, and names Francesco Cavalli as her teacher.

sources.title: Beth L. Glixon, “Strozzi, Barbara”, Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani 94 (2019)
Mario Ruffini, “Barbara Strozzi nel Novecento” (2005): the dedication, dated Venetia il 1 di Giugno 1651

places.name: Venice, Cantate, ariette a una, due e tre voci
places.what: Her third book, printed by Gardano with the dedication Ignotae deae.
places.work: Cantate, ariette a una, due e tre voci, Op. 3

sources.title: Beth L. Glixon, “Strozzi, Barbara”, Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani 94 (2019)
Mario Ruffini, “Barbara Strozzi nel Novecento” (2005): list of publications

places.name: Venice, Sacri musicali affetti
places.what: Her fifth book, devotional pieces for solo voice, printed by Francesco Magni and dedicated to Anna de’ Medici, Archduchess of Austria.

sources.title: Beth L. Glixon, “Strozzi, Barbara”, Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani 94 (2019)
IMSLP: Sacri musicali affetti, Op. 5 (Venice: Francesco Magni, 1655)

places.name: Venice, Sacra corona
places.what: Her motet Quis dabit mihi, for alto, tenor and bass, was printed as the first three-voice motet in Bartolomeo Marcesso’s anthology Sacra corona.

sources.title: Susan Clermont, “Barbara Strozzi at 400”, In The Muse (Library of Congress, 17 September 2019)
Library of Congress: Sacra corona (Venice, 1656)

places.name: Venice, Ariette a voce sola
places.what: Her sixth book, printed by Francesco Magni and dedicated to Prince Francesco Carafa.

sources.title: Beth L. Glixon, “Strozzi, Barbara”, Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani 94 (2019)
IMSLP: Ariette a voce sola, Op. 6 (Venice: Francesco Magni, 1657)

places.name: Venice, Diporti di Euterpe
places.what: Her seventh book, printed by Francesco Magni and dedicated to Nicolò Sagredo, procurator of San Marco, the only Venetian dedicatee of her books. Only two complete copies survive.

sources.title: Library of Congress: Diporti di Evterpe (Venice: Francesco Magni, 1659), title page and catalogue record
Susan Clermont, “Barbara Strozzi at 400”, In The Muse (Library of Congress, 2019)
Beth L. Glixon, “Strozzi, Barbara”, Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani 94 (2019)

places.name: Venice, Arie
places.what: Her eighth and last known book, printed by Francesco Magni and dedicated to Sophia, Duchess of Brunswick-Lüneburg, who visited Venice that year.

sources.title: Beth L. Glixon, “Strozzi, Barbara”, Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani 94 (2019)
IMSLP: Arie, Op. 8 (Venice: Francesco Magni, 1664)

places.name: Padua
places.what: Died in Padua after three months of illness.

sources.title: Beth L. Glixon, “Strozzi, Barbara”, Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani 94 (2019), citing Glixon, “More on the Life and Death of Barbara Strozzi”, Musical Quarterly 83 (1999)
Wikipedia coordinate record: Padua

places.name: Church of the Eremitani, Padua
places.what: Buried in the church of the Eremitani. The burial date is not given in the source consulted.

sources.title: Beth L. Glixon, “Strozzi, Barbara”, Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani 94 (2019)
Wikipedia coordinate record: Church of the Eremitani

places.name: Palazzo Strozzi, Florence
places.what: Posthumous performance. Luigi Dallapiccola’s orchestration of her canzonetta Amor dormiglione was played in the Concerto di musiche medicee of the sixth Maggio Musicale Fiorentino, conducted by Luigi Colonna.

sources.title: Mario Ruffini, “Barbara Strozzi nel Novecento” (Centro Studi Luigi Dallapiccola, 2005), pp. 217–218 and 227
